entities.evidence: The divine name יַהְוֶה identifies the speaker whose word comes to Abram in the vision.
אֶל אַבְרָם names the recipient of the vision as Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham.
Yahweh addresses the recipient of the vision directly by the same name, אַבְרָם.

analysis.morphology: Preposition with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה means “after these events.” The phrase points back to what has already happened and places Abram’s vision after it.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine plural noun in the absolute state. The following demonstrative הָאֵלֶּה agrees with it.

analysis.evidence: In אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה, “after these events,” הָאֵלֶּה agrees with הַדְּבָרִים in number and definiteness and points back to the events just recounted.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes אֵלֶּה, a common-gender plural demonstrative used attributively after הַדְּבָרִים.

analysis.evidence: אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה places the event after the preceding events. הָיָה דְבַר יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם reports that the word of Yahweh came to Abram, and לֵאמֹר introduces what Yahweh said.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, agreeing with the subject דְבַר יַהְוֶה. The verb has no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: דְבַר יַהְוֶה identifies Yahweh as the source of the message, and אֶל אַבְרָם identifies Abram as its recipient. לֵאמֹר introduces the message itself, beginning with אַל תִּירָא אַבְרָם, “Do not fear, Abram.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with יַהְוֶה as its complement.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

draft.change: Add Genesis 15:7 as an example of the existing sense to-a-person-speaking for אֶל.
draft.definition: With a verb of speaking, אֶל marks the person addressed.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 15:7, וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו introduces Yahweh’s words to Abram. The third-person suffix names the addressee from the narrator’s perspective, and Yahweh addresses him in the second person in הוֹצֵאתִיךָ.

analysis.evidence: In הָיָה דְבַר יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם, אֶל introduces Abram as the recipient of Yahweh’s word. The direct address אַל תִּירָא אַבְרָם (“Do not fear, Abram”) confirms that Yahweh is speaking to him.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In אֶל אַבְרָם (“to Abram”), the marked name identifies the recipient of Yahweh’s word. The name recurs in direct address in אַל תִּירָא אַבְרָם (“Do not fear, Abram”).
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with no prefix or suffix. The preceding preposition אֶל is a separate word.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: Yahweh’s word comes to Abram בַּמַּחֲזֶה, and לֵאמֹר introduces the words Abram hears. The phrase identifies the vision as the setting of the revelation.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ ‘in’ combines with the definite article to form בַּ, doubling the noun’s initial מ. The noun is masculine singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67848:7, 67599:4, 66845:4, 66321:11, 66064:5, 65814:3.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with prefixed preposition לְ, realized as לֵ־

analysis.evidence: In אַל תִּירָא אַבְרָם, “Do not fear, Abram,” אַל negates the second-person singular verb תִּירָא. The following promise, “I am a shield for you,” gives Abram a reason to heed this reassuring command.
analysis.morphology: Negative particle with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Negates a command addressed to Abram.

analysis.evidence: אַל תִּירָא אַבְרָם means “Do not be afraid, Abram.” The words אָנֹכִי מָגֵן לָךְ (“I am a shield for you”) reassure Abram of protection.
analysis.morphology: Qal jussive, second person masculine singular, addressed to Abram. The separate particle אַל marks the prohibition.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: The verse first names Abram as the recipient of Yahweh’s word (אֶל אַבְרָם). In אַל תִּירָא אַבְרָם, “Do not fear, Abram,” Yahweh addresses him by name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun used in direct address, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67332:4, 66569:12, 66314:8.
analysis.morphology: Independent personal pronoun, first person common singular, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After telling Abram אַל תִּירָא, “do not fear,” Yahweh says אָנֹכִי מָגֵן לָךְ, “I am a shield for you.” The shield image identifies Yahweh as Abram’s protector.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of both genders, singular absolute. It serves as the predicate of אָנֹכִי and has no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 15:1 as an example of the existing le-dative sense.
draft.definition: לְ marks the person for whose benefit something is done.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 15:1 Yahweh tells Abram, אָנֹכִי מָגֵן לָךְ, “I am a shield for you.” Abram receives the protection.

analysis.evidence: In אָנֹכִי מָגֵן לָךְ, “I am a shield for you,” לָךְ identifies Abram as the person Yahweh protects. אַל תִּירָא אַבְרָם addresses him with a masculine singular verb, and שְׂכָרְךָ, “your reward,” resumes the same address with an explicit masculine singular suffix.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ takes a second-person masculine singular pronominal suffix. לָךְ is the pausal form of לְךָ at the end of the clause.
analysis.sense: Marks the person for whom the speaker serves as a shield.

analysis.evidence: YHWH addresses Abram directly. The suffix ךָ identifies Abram as the recipient, and הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד describes his reward as very great.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with a second-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Abram.

analysis.evidence: In שְׂכָרְךָ הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד, הַרְבֵּה describes the size of Abram’s reward, and מְאֹד intensifies it. The phrase means “your reward is very great.”
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive absolute used predicatively to express quantity. The initial הַ is part of the verbal stem.
